einzeiler: Analyzing the staggering financial costs of the Iran war and Pentagon opacity.
kurzfassung: Stephen Semler breaks down the unprecedented unpopularity and astronomical financial costs of the U.S. war with Iran. He reveals how the defense budget exceeds $1.1 trillion while key government agencies and the Pentagon stonewall transparency. The discussion also examines the immense financial and military support provided to Israel and its impact on American taxpayers.
stichpunkte: The U.S. war with Iran is the most unpopular conflict in modern polling history.
The enacted defense budget for fiscal year 2026 reached an unprecedented $1.1 trillion.
More than half of the annual military budget flows directly to for-profit defense contractors.
Members of Congress who receive more money from arms companies are significantly more likely to vote for military budget increases.
The Pentagon has never passed a financial audit and routinely stonewalls independent cost assessments.
The Congressional Budget Office estimated war costs at $38 billion, a figure heavily criticized as drastically underestimated.
Cumulative U.S. aid to Israel since its founding has reached $352 billion in constant terms.

clips.hook: The Iran war started with negative support and reached negative 35 net approval.
clips.text: The discussion highlights that unlike previous major conflicts that began with positive public backing, the war with Iran started with net negative support and plummeted over time.

clips.hook: Post-9/11 war costs have skyrocketed well above three trillion dollars.
clips.text: The dialogue examines how post-9/11 military expenditures have spiraled into trillions of dollars, creating a massive financial burden alongside indirect economic impacts.

beschreibung:
We’re spending more a year on the military in adjusted dollars than we did during World War II. What are we getting for it? And how much is going to Israel? Stephen Semler has the numbers.
